hook.line: Don Hernando says what everyone is good at, and what he has already suffered, without naming either. Spanish uses one small word for "my thing" or "my share".

examples.en: I've already been through my share.
What we had did not work out.

examples.es: Lo mío es escribir, no hablar.
examples.en: Writing is my thing, not talking.

rule:
*Lo* plus a possessive points at "what is mine, yours, theirs" and leaves the thing vague on purpose.

*Lo mío*, *lo tuyo*, *lo suyo*, *lo nuestro*.

Two common meanings:

*Lo tuyo es…* means "your thing is", what you are good at.

*Pasé lo mío* or *sufrió lo suyo* means "my share" or "her share" of trouble.

*Lo* never changes for gender or number: *lo mío*, never *la mía* here.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the neuter article with a stressed possessive.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ es la cocina.* (*Lo tuyo* or *Lo mío*) Cooking is your thing (to a friend).
yourTurn.why: You is *tú*, so the thing is *tuyo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Yo ya pasé ___.* (*lo mío* or *lo suyo*) I've already been through my share.
yourTurn.why: I am the one who suffered, so the share is *mío*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: My grandmother suffered her share.
yourTurn.why: *Suyo* is about her, and *lo* stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Writing is my thing, not talking.
yourTurn.answer: Lo mío es escribir, no hablar.
yourTurn.why: *Lo mío es* plus the thing you are good at.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: What we had did not work out.
yourTurn.why: *Lo nuestro* is the vague "what we had".

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Everyone mind their own business.
yourTurn.why: *A lo suyo* means to their own thing.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Vale: *Yo ya pasé lo mío.* becomes: Vale has already been through her share.
yourTurn.why: For Vale it is *suyo*, and the verb ends in *-ó*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish says "the yours" here: *lo tuyo* instead of "your thing".
*Lo* never changes, so the possessive stays *mío*.
The *lo* stays in front of the possessive.

personal: What is your thing? Say it with *Lo mío es…* and add what your family has already been through: *Mi familia pasó lo suyo.*
